title: Training Notes: The Home-Sale Contingency and the Kick-Out Notice (Home Purchase Agreement)
content:
**When may a Home Purchase Agreement be contingent on the sale of the buyer's current home?**
Only where the collection allows a home-sale contingency. Its deadline is the contract date plus the collection's contingency days.

**What is a kick-out notice?**
When Calloway accepts a backup offer on the homesite, it sends the buyer a kick-out notice.

**How long does the buyer have after a kick-out notice?**
The contingency must be released within the collection's kick-out response days (calendar days) after the kick-out notice was sent. Counting starts the day after the notice date and the last counted day is included. The dates are read from the kick-out notice entry on the agreement ledger.

**What happens if the buyer releases in time?**
The agreement continues without the contingency.

**And otherwise?**
If the buyer does not release in time, and also when the contingency deadline passes unsatisfied, the buyer's cancellation with basis kick-out or sale contingency not met refunds every deposit except the lot premium deposit, which is refunded only where the collection marks the lot premium deposit as refundable.

**A worked boundary (hypothetical dates).** A kick-out notice is sent on 10 June on an agreement whose collection allows 3 days. The counted days are 11, 12 and 13 June. A release on 13 June is in time and the agreement continues without the contingency; on 14 June the release is not in time.

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Contingency released within the kick-out response days | Agreement continues without it |
| Not released in time after a kick-out notice, buyer cancels with basis kick-out | Every deposit refunded except the lot premium deposit, which follows the collection's refundability |
| Contingency deadline passes unsatisfied, buyer cancels with basis sale contingency not met | Every deposit refunded except the lot premium deposit, which follows the collection's refundability |
